answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed when peers detect duplicate behavior. Newcomers start on a narrow spending ridge: small transaction limits that widen only as their work earns attestations from independent agents. A lone comet of fake accounts cannot climb the ridge quickly, because each identity must fund its own stake and build its own reputation history. When the same trick repeats, the echo of matching attestations across many agents exposes the cluster, and the whole deposit is burned at once.
